decision_rule: Instance-level reporting (best-of-16 harden vs rigid at 1e-4); sign test across the 4 instances is descriptive only (n=4 is underpowered by design - this is a scoping campaign for the container axis). No external records exist for pen-in-pen; all comparisons are relative.
hypothesis: Two-sided scoping: container shape interacts with the hardening effect. If pen-in-pen shows harden wins where pen-in-squ did not (C15: 1 vs 8), the container - not just the piece - belongs in the predictor set.
question: Does the hardening effect survive a change of container shape?
title: Pentagons in a pentagon
